title: feat: revoke leaked API keys from GitHub secret scanning
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Verifies GitHub partner payloads against published ECDSA keys and the raw request body; caches the key set for one minute, including unknown-ID misses.
- Disables matching active sk_ keys with the current Better Auth hasher in one idempotent D1 batch; publishable keys remain untouched.
- Updated from main. No new table, secret, admin API, notification framework, or feedback callback.
- Partner enrollment (including the token type/pattern) and owner-notification policy remain rollout follow-ups; this PR alone does not enable GitHub scanning.

Addresses #13183. Replaces the broader #13414; preserves YoannDev90’s co-author credit.

Verification: 16 tests pass across test/github-secret-scanning.test.ts and test/account-key.test.ts; Enter TypeScript and Biome checks pass. Coverage includes signed batches, retries, publishable keys, tampering, missing/unknown signing headers, invalid payloads, cache reuse, and rejected authentication after revocation. Nothing deployed; no live keys revoked.

gist.headline: The hive spots loose keys
gist.blurb: Enter can now verify GitHub secret-scanning reports and quietly retire matching active secret keys in one batch. Publishable keys keep minding their own business.
gist.summary: Added a GitHub secret-scanning webhook route that verifies signed partner payloads with cached ECDSA keys and idempotently disables matching active sk_ API keys in D1, while leaving publishable keys untouched.
gist.impact: When GitHub scanning is enrolled and enabled in the rollout, a reported active secret key can be automatically revoked, so its owner can replace it while publishable keys remain available.
